status_reason: Both experiments' designs, timings (1.2-s digits, 2.0-s delay, 3.7 s from response to next digit), trial counts and test-stimulus rules follow the paper; the changes are apparatus substitutions (keys for levers, an on-screen disc for the lamp) and the undescribed payoff scheme left out, all listed as deviations. Everything the paper leaves unstated is in the 'Assumed, not in the paper' table. No participant data: software verification only.

original.citation: Sternberg, S. (1966). High-speed scanning in human memory. Science, 153(3736), 652-654.

notes: Two tasks: memory-scanning (experiment 1) and memory-scanning-fixed (experiment 2). The paper's own results (slopes 37.9 and 38.3 ms per digit, intercepts 397.2 and 369.4 ms) are quoted for comparison only; this folder has recorded no participant data.
